title: Vector ingress smoothing and kernel grace prefetch to reduce embedding p99
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our vector embedding endpoint shows sporadic p99 spikes for short requests (<64 tokens) under mixed traffic. Root causes observed: microburst arrival patterns that create tiny batches (1-3 requests), kernel cold-start work (JIT/kernel selection), and KV cache cold reads for tenant shards. These spikes increase tail latency by 2-4x during load bursts and harm customer SLAs for low-latency features (search, rerank).

Goal: Reduce p99 latency for embedding endpoint for short-sequence requests by 25-40% without materially reducing steady-state throughput or increasing cost >5%. Approach combines an ingress shaping window (time-based smoothing), a short reservoir to coalesce near-simultaneous requests, and a kernel "grace prefetch" warm pool so the runtime can prebind kernels and KV state for predicted tiny batches. Also add telemetry and gating to revert if throughput/regression observed.

Scope: Changes limited to the embedding ingress and scheduler code and a small runtime kernel-warm pool layer. No model changes. Feature gated per-deployment and canaryed on a subset of vector endpoints (dev & staging then prod bucket).
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings with input length <64 reduced by >=30% in the canary workload (3 representative tenants)
p50 and p95 show no regression >5% vs baseline under same load profile
end-to-end throughput loss under sustained load <5%
no significant cost increase (per-token cost delta <2%)
feature deployable behind runtime feature flag and rollout plan defined
dashboard shows per-tenant p50/p95/p99, kernel-warmpool hit rate, and ingress-hold rate
tasks: Bench: reproduce tail spikes locally with traffic replay (use 3 tenant traces) and record baseline p50/p95/p99
Design: finalize ingress smoothing window heuristic (time cap, max-hold-ms, adaptive backoff based on queue depth)
Implement: ingress reservoir + short hold (configurable 1-10ms) with per-tenant cap
Implement: kernel grace prefetch pool (N warm kernel slots per GPU), integrate with scheduler kernel selector
Telemetry: add histograms for hold-time, coalesced-batch-size, kernel-warm-hit, kv-prefetch-misses
Load test: synthetic burst tests (Poisson bursts and heavy tail), A/B canary runs in staging
Safety: add fail-open fastpath (bypass hold) and circuit-breaker when queue depth exceeds threshold
PRs: create runtime and scheduler PRs, tests, and perf regression tests
Rollout: canary 5% of production traffic, monitor 24h, then 25% then full
Postmortem: collect results and update runbook with rollback criteria
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage. Collected traces from grafana: vector-endpoint/region-eu/p99 spikes correlate with microbursts during customer ingest windows. Created reproducer and baseline metrics. Refer Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-863210+ingress+prefetch

2026-03-03 - Jordan Li: Proposed 'hold-for-coalesce' heuristic: hold up to 6ms or until batch >=8. Added adaptive shortening when queue grows. Flagged potential risk of increased tail under pathological bursts if hold window misconfigured.

2026-03-06 - Design review with PM (Maya Patel): PM happy with 6ms default but requested per-tenant control and telemetry for user-visible SLOs. Suggested acceptance criteria include cost delta limits.

2026-03-09 - Engineering note: Implemented prototype of ingress reservoir and microbench. Observed kernel startup reduced by ~60% for coalesced batches in microbench but KV prefetch still necessary for some tenants. Added kv-prefetch heuristic (tenant-shard warm tokens) to next sprint.

2026-03-11 - Perf run (staging): p99 improved 28% for short inputs in Poisson burst test, throughput steady. Kernel-warm-hit reported 86% after 2m of warm-up. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1942
2026-03-12 - Security/Infra: Confirmed no new privileged surfaces. KMS/HSM unaffected. Security review not required for this change.

2026-03-13 - Ops: Added Grafana panels: /grafana/d/embedding-latency, and a runbook snippet for rollback if p99 worsens or if spike in queued requests > 1k for >5m. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embedding-latency

2026-03-14 - QA: Running extended soak for 48h on canary. Early signal: p99 stable, but observed rare stalls when hold window combined with GPU backpressure. Mitigation: tighten circuit-breaker threshold and reduce max-hold-ms to 4ms for canary.
dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-prefetch - shard hit-rate and prefetch latency
notes: Tradeoffs: Time-based holding reduces kernel cold overhead but introduces a small added delay in median latency for some single-request flows. We minimize this by capping hold window and by allowing bypass when queue/backpressure is high.
Fallback: If kernel warmpool hit rate < 50% or queued requests > configured threshold, system bypasses hold and fastpath is used to protect throughput.
Next steps if successful: extend approach to reranking endpoints and to dedicated capacity pools with per-tenant warm zones.
Related: see ENG-341210 for Packet coalescer autotune and ENG-452368 for KV slice prefetch telemetry
